summary: Every acceptance settle-path that should hold DID hold: agent-made, self-approval, recomputed-digest mismatch, absent/None displayed digest, short quorum, irreversible/money/external without two_key, non-list malformed impact (fails closed to two-key-required), conflicting (accept+reject) changelog, unresolvable actor, idless terminal entry, no attributable opening, INERT policy=None, and absent digest_reader ALL returned settle=0 (held/skipped) with a named reason - no acceptance fail-open found. Actor, intent, proposer, and changelog_id are derived ONLY from the ordered attributed changelog; record.get('status') is read solely by the open/skip gate and never drives the decision; the module reads no self-declared decision field (decided_by/proposed_by/producer appear only as WRITES into the settlement record, set to the changelog-verified actor). All 7 teeth (T-agent, T-proposer, T-digest, T-cas re-run, T-cas duplicate, T-conflict, T-authorized) were independently re-mutated from source and confirmed NON-VACUOUS (mutant settles 1 or 2, real holds 0 or 1, .warp/request_reconcile.py on-disk sha256 unchanged after each). The digest recompute is genuinely the module's OWN guard: is_authorized cannot catch a forged displayed digest because _build_attestation binds the attestation's bound_digest TO that same displayed digest, so the module's recompute==displayed check is the sole forged-binding catch (T-digest confirms). Frozen safety core (authorization/two_key/policy_check/decision) is byte-UNCHANGED (absent from the diff and git-diff-clean vs parent) and composed with caller-supplied VERIFIED identities. The reconcile calls the adapter ONLY for read_changelog (no write method) so it writes NO tracker state (write audit empty after a run); the shipped policy.yaml carries no human_decisions block so the engine is INERT and a valid transition is HELD under policy=None; no daemon/timer/poller/thread/network exists and main() exposes only selfcheck. Gate GREEN (5 run / 18 na), selftest 2658 passed / 0 failed, 8 capabilities.yaml copies one sha256. The notes cover the deliberate rejection-path design (fail-safe, but it bypasses safety-core validation - a documented choice for the surface owner to confirm), a reference-store (never gate-run) event-append durability edge for WARP-0620, and two review-lane shape advisories; none is a fail-open and none blocks landing.

findings.text: REJECTION PATH (builder-flagged, confirmed fail-SAFE, not a fail-open). A terminal rejection settles a warp.approval/warp.decision/warp.verdict record + request.rejected event guarded ONLY by the machine-actor check - is_authorized, the repo-digest recompute, two_key, quorum, and separation are all skipped. Confirmed by probe: a rejection by an unknown/unauthorized/non-registry non-machine human SETTLES (settle=1), including when the request is irreversible and when the displayed digest is forged. This is defensible - a rejection authorizes NO action and cannot make anything proceed (verified: no decision.decided emitted on reject, only request.rejected), so it moves in the fail-safe direction, and the machine-actor guard blocks the automation (the primary attacker) from fabricating rejections. Residual, worth the surface owner's explicit sign-off: (1) an unauthorized-but-non-machine board user can settle a rejection that closes a request (downstream W3 sets terminal status, after which later valid acceptances are skipped) - a DoS/veto vector, mitigated by board access control (WARP-0614 fences); (2) the rejection settlement record names the actor as the decider and carries bound_digest = the UNVERIFIED displayed digest (the reject path never recomputes), a minor audit-integrity wrinkle. Recommend the surface owner confirm rejections intentionally require only the machine-actor guard; if audit integrity matters, recompute the digest and record it as unverified on the reject path.

REFERENCE STORE DURABILITY (out of gate scope, for WARP-0620). FilesystemSettlementStore._apply (never gate-run) writes the settlement file FIRST (correct per AC4), then appends events, then appends the receipt LAST. A crash between the event append and the receipt append would, on retry (no receipt yet), re-append the event(s) to .warp/events.jsonl - at-least-once rather than exactly-once event emission. The gate proves idempotency over the in-memory FakeSettlementStore (atomic), and the builder documents a single-writer poll-when-run discipline; the live shape is WARP-0620's. Flagging so WARP-0620 makes the receipt write the atomic commit point (e.g. receipt-first-with-fsync, or a single atomic append) rather than events-then-receipt.

SHAPE REVIEW-LANE ADVISORIES (gate GREEN, non-blocking by design). verify.sh reports _reconcile_one cyclomatic complexity 28 (> 20 budget) and .warp/tracker_adapter.py 15% duplicated lines (> 8% budget), both review-lane advisory not gate-enforced. The complexity is an inherent linear chain of fail-closed guards (each a distinct refusal with a named reason), which is appropriate for a safety gate; the adapter duplication is read_changelog mirroring the existing read_item/seed pattern. No action required to land; noted for a future readability pass.
